CYGNET (codename Duckling) — prototype build
============================================

A cozy game about a duckling who is not a duckling. This is an early
vertical slice: one pond, Act 1, and a flight playground. It is not
finished, it has no menu, and it will not save your progress.


RUNNING IT
----------

Windows:  unzip anywhere, double-click Cygnet.exe.
          Windows SmartScreen will warn that the publisher is unknown —
          the build is not code-signed. Click "More info" -> "Run anyway".
Linux:    unzip, then  chmod +x Cygnet.x86_64  and run it.

Alt+Enter toggles fullscreen. Alt+F4 (or Esc then close) quits.


CONTROLS
--------

  W A S D        walk / swim / steer in the air
  Mouse          camera   (Esc releases the mouse to the desktop)
  Space          hop on land, flap in the air — hold to climb
  W / S in air   pull up / dive
  Shift          run
  E              talk to whoever the prompt names, pick things up
  R              look at yourself


WHAT TO TRY
-----------

You start inside the egg. Mash Space to peck your way out, then follow
Marra when she calls. Keep up with the family across the pond, say hello
to all five of them, catch the water bugs at supper, and hide when a
shadow crosses the water. After that the pond goes quiet — find the mouse
on the far shore and collect eight seeds for him.

One of the supper bugs is on the other side of the culvert pipe, on the
west bank. You fit through it. Remember that you did.


DEBUG KEYS (left in on purpose, for poking around)
--------------------------------------------------

  G        force a growth spurt
  [ and ]  step the growth stage down / up
  F1       jump to the pond
  F2       jump to the flight playground (fly through the rings)

The overlay in the top-left is a developer readout, not the real HUD.


WHAT I'D LIKE TO KNOW
---------------------

- Did anything block you that looked like it should have let you through?
- Did you find the bug through the culvert without being told twice?
- Later on, when the pipe is too small for you — does that register as
  something you lost, or just as a wall?
- Did the family ever leave you behind, or feel like they were waiting
  too obviously?
- When the colour drains out of the pond, does it land?
- Is flying fun?
